[Problem]{.card-kicker} **Maximum Points You Can Obtain from Cards** [LC 1423 · Maximum Points You Can Obtain from Cards](https://leetcode.com/problems/maximum-points-you-can-obtain-from-cards/){difficulty="Medium"}

After $k$ picks, whatever is left is a single **contiguous** run of $n-k$ cards in the middle: taking $i$ from the left and $k-i$ from the right leaves the block `cardPoints[i .. i+(n-k)-1]`. So maximising the taken score is the same as **minimising the sum of a fixed-size window of $n-k$ cards** — the complement. The total is fixed, so $\text{score} = \text{total} - \text{smallest middle window}$. This turns a two-ended greedy-sounding problem into exactly the fixed-size slide of @sec-sw-p1-a, pointed the other way.

[Solved in full in @sec-sw-p1-b.]{.card-link}

:::
